data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2022 the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding was $724.298m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle (2018-2020 columns) shows a net adverse prior-year development of $29.6m (approx. 4.09% of opening gross reserves), driven primarily by upward development in the 2019 and 2020 underwriting years. The movement reflects large-loss and catastrophe-related development (including prior years' hurricanes, wildfires and pandemic-related exposures), inflationary pressures and specific IBNR allowances taken for the Russia/Ukraine conflict. The report also highlights pockets of favourable prior-year development in classes such as Property D&F, Marine Hull, Marine Energy, Non-Marine Liability and Political Risk, but on aggregate the gross triangle shows a net strengthening of reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: Included within net calendar year claims incurred of $193,957,000 (2021: $196,366,000) is a release of $7,883,000 in claims reserves established for losses incurred at the prior year end (2021: release $7,832,000).

The calendar year result also benefitted from favourable incurred claims development on prior accident years from a number of classes, including Property D&F, Marine Hull, Marine Energy, Non-Marine Liability and Political Risk.
We have made specific incurred but not reported ("IBNR") allowances for classes where there is potential for losses arising as a result of the ongoing Russia/Ukraine conflict.
The total net cost to Syndicate 1969 of these allowances for the 2022 calendar year is $4.8m.
The total net cost to the syndicate of these events for the 2022 calendar year exceeded the catastrophe allowance for the calendar year by $3.8m.
Inflation, in all its forms including social inflation, continues to be a key theme of discussion and has been specifically factored into our reserving this year.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development was calculated from the published gross claims development triangle (gross incurred cumulative amounts) at 31 Dec 2022 by comparing each older underwriting year's current estimate to the previous diagonal (excludes 2021 and 2022). The report also contains a net prior-year release sentence ($7.883m release) in the Technical Provisions note; that net figure (after reinsurance) differs from the gross triangle-derived adverse movement of $29.6m. No explicit gross single-line 'movement in prior year's provision' amount was provided, so the gross triangle was used as the primary source. SPA/RITC transactions are noted elsewhere in the report (could distort some comparatives), and per the document 2017 & prior gross claims were reinsured out in 2021 which affects comparability of older columns. Amounts and percentages are in the report's native currency (USD millions).
